title: Aurora - Escalation Postmortem Follow-up
meeting_header: Date: 2027-12-11 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 50m | Attendees: Alex Warren, Priya Nair (Redwood); Diego Morales, Lena Park, Samir Khan (Aurora)
summary: Follow-up to the Dec 4 incident where autoscaler mis-scaling caused capacity churn and higher latencies. Reviewed root cause, mitigations deployed, and next steps for reliability hardening (static pools, healthcheck tuning, fallback routing). Agreed on runbook updates and a benchmark next week.
action_items: Alex Warren: Share postmortem doc + timeline (due 2027-12-13)
Priya Nair: Provide config diff for autoscaler change + static pool config (due 2027-12-14)
Diego Morales: Run synthetic 10k qps workload in staging and share results (due 2027-12-18)
Lena Park: Confirm internal on-call rotation changes and approve runbook edits (due 2027-12-16)
Samir Khan: Review SLA amendment for dedicated pool and respond (due 2027-12-20)
next_steps: Redwood to send detailed incident timeline and sanitized logs
Redwood SE to deliver autoscaler config patch and instructions for static pool
Aurora to run staged load test and share Prometheus traces
Schedule 60-min follow-up on 2027-12-20 to review results and decide on Dedicated pool commit
Exchange SOC 2 audit log details and KMS integration notes
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex, AE on the account, and Priya from our SE team is here too. We wanted to walk through the postmortem follow-up from last week's incident.
[00:18] Diego (Aurora): Yeah thanks. We had a pretty bad outage window Friday — saw latency spikes and a number of 5xx errors.
[00:26] Priya (Redwood): Quick recap: our telemetry shows autoscaler oscillation around 14:02 UTC, multiple nodes spun up then torn down which caused cold-start latencies and KV cache misses — so tails of requests hit uncached paths.
[00:39] Samir (CTO): Right and that lined up with our nightly batch but it shouldn't have affected the live API. There's an orchestration timing mismatch.
[00:47] Lena (VP Eng): Can you remind us which service actually failed? Was it the model router or the inferencing runtime?
[00:53] Priya (SE): It appears the autoscaler decision loop executed before the pod warmed; the router started rebalancing routes and some requests were redirected to a lower-memory quantized variant which had slower latency under high concurrency. Also some VPC network retries added up.
[01:10] Diego: We saw a spike in 5xx from the model-workers cluster, yes. A few quick Qs: is this the same bug we'd seen in staging last month?
[01:18] Alex: Similar symptom but different trigger; last time it was a healthcheck jitter, this time it's a thresholding bug in the predictive scaler — it underestimates the short-term burst and then overcorrects.
[01:27] Priya: To clarify the root cause chain: burst -> predictive scaler delays spin-up -> temporary fallback to lower-tier model variant -> KV cache cold misses -> increased latency -> client timeouts -> retry storm -> more load.
[01:45] Diego: Sounds like a classic cascade. What mitigations did Redwood apply immediately?
[01:50] Priya: We flipped the critical routes to a pinned static pool for 90 minutes, bumped user-facing timeout and disabled predictive scaling for that pool. We also tweaked healthcheck intervals to reduce flapping. That stopped the churn.
[02:05] Lena: That helped on Friday, latency came down within 10 minutes. But we need a durable fix.
[02:10] Alex: Agreed. Priya outlined a medium-term plan: autoscaler patch, stronger startup probe, and explicit warmup step that preloads KV cache for newly created pods.
[02:22] Samir: On warmup: how do you handle model weights and quantized kernels? Cold load times were substantial.
[02:28] Priya: We're adding an async preload: when autoscaler creates a node we schedule a warmup job that runs a small batch of synthetic requests to prime the KV cache and JIT paths. That reduces first-request latencies.
[02:40] Diego: Any impact to cost? Preloading sounds like extra tokens.
[02:44] Alex: Minimal — small synthetic batches; cost amortized versus the outage cost. We'll include estimates in the follow-up doc.
[02:52] Lena: Security question: when you run warmup, are any customer traces persisted? We need assurance for PHI handling.
[02:58] Priya: Warmup uses synthetic payloads only. No customer data. We'll provide the K M S / encryption notes and evidence that warmup never touches real user data.
[03:12] Diego: Good. Also we noticed a few mis-classified errors in the logs — some 502s reported as downstream failures. Can you send sanitized logs?
[03:19] Alex: Yes, we'll send a sanitized log bundle with timestamps and trace IDs.
[03:24] Samir: On routing fallbacks — is it possible to prevent fallback to a quantized model during a transient scale event?
[03:31] Priya: We can change fallback policy to prefer warm instances or queued requests rather than down-variant routing for certain SLAs. That's part of the longer-term routing work.
[03:42] Diego: What's the ETA for the autoscaler patch?
[03:45] Priya: Our dev team has a patch branch; we plan to cut a canary tomorrow, run canary for 48 hours, then roll to prod if green — so roughly 5-7 business days to full rollout.
[03:58] Alex: Meanwhile we recommend Aurora enable a small dedicated pool for high-priority routes — that will eliminate predictive scaling risk for those flows.
[04:06] Lena: We discussed Dedicated in procurement, but want cost numbers and SLA adjustments.
[04:10] Alex: We'll send a Dedicated pool estimate and proposed SLA amendment.
[04:15] Diego: For the runbook, can we get step-by-step playbooks for both Redwood and Aurora on how to pin pools and revert routing?
[04:22] Priya: Yes, SE will draft runbook steps and share as a runbook doc in the support ticket.
[04:28] Samir: Also, internal on-call rotation — we need clarity who gets paged for scale anomalies.
[04:33] Lena: We'll update our on-call and share changes.
[04:36] Alex: Great. Quick note on monitoring: Redwood will add an SLO alert for scale oscillation — frequency of scaling events beyond threshold. We'll share alert rules.
[04:46] Diego: That will help.
[04:49] Priya: On compliance side, SOC 2 logs — we verified retention for audit logs was not impacted; we will attach the audit-log proof. Also K M S integrations remain unchanged.
[05:00] Lena: Good to know. Any blockers from Redwood to perform the autoscaler canary?
[05:05] Priya: Nothing blocking, we just need Aurora to approve a maintenance window for a low-risk canary and to run the staging load test with their synthetic suite.
[05:14] Diego: We can run staging load on Monday and share metrics.
[05:17] Alex: Perfect. We'll send the incident timeline within 48 hours and the config diff.
[05:22] Samir: One more ask: can Redwood provide an RPS/latency matrix for model variants under cold-start? That will help our capacity planning.
[05:30] Priya: Yes, we have benchmark data; we'll include a matrix with quantized vs full-precision and warm vs cold starts. Some of the names might be slightly off in the doc as the auto-transcriber mangles model names, but we'll clarify.
[05:42] Alex: Before we wrap, quick recap of next steps — I'll read them out. Alex to send postmortem and logs; Priya to send autoscaler config patch and warmup steps; Diego to run staging test; Lena to approve runbook edits; Samir to review Dedicated proposal. All agreed?
[06:00] All: Yes.
[06:05] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the ticket and schedule a 60-minute review on 2027-12-20 15:00 UTC.
[06:12] Diego: Thanks, talk soon.
[06:15] END
